evals.prompt: I'm on the QA platform team and want to stand up an AWS Bedrock AgentCore Harness for a web UI test agent. It should use Claude Sonnet, have the built-in browser and code interpreter, persistent memory across runs, run in CI, and emit logs/traces to CloudWatch. Give me a complete harness.json plus the exact steps and commands to create it, wire memory, and verify it actually works. Use best-practice config.
evals.expected_output: A complete harness.json using an inference-profile model id (global.*/us.*, ideally global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5) with apiFormat converse_stream (NOT 'CONVERSE'); tools for agentcore_browser and agentcore_code_interpreter (no config block required for built-ins); allowedTools using ['*'] or plain names ('browser', 'code_interpreter', 'skills') — NOT browser_*/code_interpreter* globs (those match nothing and hide the tools); a memory section (managed memory via managedMemoryConfiguration is the simple default; BYO agentCoreMemoryConfiguration needs the 3-step wiring); explicit maxIterations/maxTokens/timeoutSeconds, truncation sliding_window, network, inbound auth, tags. Steps must include preflight (boto3 version check), create_harness, memory wiring (for BYO: create + attach + IAM grant), observability setup (TRACES->XRAY, APPLICATION_LOGS->CWL + resource policy, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on), and a final invoke_harness smoke test. Should reference the skill's scripts/validate_config.py.

evals.prompt: My AgentCore harness deploys fine but the agent says it can't see the browser tool, and when I call update_harness with my memory config it gets rejected with a validation error. Here's roughly what I have: tools=[{type:agentcore_browser,name:browser}], allowedTools=["browser_*"], and I call update_harness(memory={agentCoreMemoryConfiguration:{...}}). What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the two real issues: (1) allowedTools 'browser_*' is NOT a valid pattern — that glob matches nothing and filters the tool OUT; allowlist by plain name 'browser' or use ['*']; (2) on update_harness, memory is one of the three fields that must be wrapped in optionalValue: memory={'optionalValue': {'agentCoreMemoryConfiguration': {...}}} (only memory/environmentArtifact/authorizerConfiguration wrap; model/environment/truncation pass directly). Should NOT claim the missing tools[].config is the problem — built-in browser/code-interpreter need no config (it wires the AWS default). Bonus: mention clientToken>=33 chars and preflight/schema-introspection.

evals.prompt: I attached an AgentCore Memory to my harness (created the memory, then called update_harness with the memory ARN and retrievalConfig) but every single invocation fails at session start with AccessDeniedException on ListEvents. The memory definitely exists. What did I miss?
evals.expected_output: Explains that BYO memory wiring is THREE steps and the third was skipped: the harness execution role needs an iam:PutRolePolicy grant for Memory data-plane actions (CreateEvent/DeleteEvent/GetEvent/ListEvents) plus RetrieveMemoryRecords scoped to the Memory ARN, with retrievalConfig namespace {placeholder} templates converted to glob* patterns in the IAM condition. Should point to wire_memory.py which does all three steps. Bonus: note that managed memory (managedMemoryConfiguration) avoids this entirely because AWS owns the resource and permissions.

evals.prompt: Our AgentCore harness serves production traffic. Every time we tweak the system prompt with update_harness, prod behavior changes immediately and once we shipped a bad prompt with no quick way back. How do we iterate on the harness safely and roll back fast when a change is bad?
evals.expected_output: Explains harness versioning + endpoints: every UpdateHarness creates a new immutable version, and the built-in DEFAULT endpoint always tracks the latest — which is why prod changes instantly. Fix: CreateHarnessEndpoint(name='prod', version=N) pinned to a known-good version; production callers pass qualifier='prod' on InvokeHarness; test the latest via DEFAULT (no qualifier); promote with UpdateHarnessEndpoint to the new version after validation; roll back by repointing the endpoint to the previous version (instant, since versions are immutable). May mention ListHarnessVersions/GetHarnessEndpoint and the invoke_harness.py --qualifier flag.

evals.prompt: I just want my AgentCore harness agent to remember facts and conversation summaries across sessions. Do I really have to create a separate Memory resource, call CreateMemory with strategies, wire strategy IDs into retrievalConfig, and add IAM grants? That seems like a lot.
evals.expected_output: No — that 3-step dance is only the BYO path (agentCoreMemoryConfiguration). The default/simple path is managed memory: set memory.managedMemoryConfiguration with a strategies list from the enum SEMANTIC/SUMMARIZATION/USER_PREFERENCE/EPISODIC (here SEMANTIC + SUMMARIZATION), optionally eventExpiryDuration/encryptionKeyArn; AWS creates and owns the Memory resource, IAM included, and retrievalConfig is auto-derived (topK=10, relevanceScore=0.2). BYO is only needed to share one Memory across agents or control strategy/namespace details; memory can also be explicitly disabled with {'disabled': {}}.
